title: Protection testing after a substation build

blocks.text: A transmission company builds substations and must test each new station's protection relays. The model in `testing.py` has a binary `x[pid, t]` for each project and each year `t` in its `starts`; the plan's years are `years`, and each project starts at most once (given). `testing` maps each testing project to a pair `(station, k)`, and the regulator's rule is:

items: Testing may not start before its station starts (the same year is fine).
Testing has a deadline: if the station starts in year `s`, its testing must have started by year `s + k`. This holds whether or not the planners like it: building the station commits the testing.

The plan only covers `years`. If a station's deadline `s + k` falls after the plan's last year, its testing is not required inside this plan (the next plan will take it up), though it may still be done.

blocks.text: Write `add_testing_rules(model, x, projects, years, testing)` so that the model allows exactly the plans that keep the rules.
The model so far, with $`P`$ the projects, $`Y`$ the plan's years and $`T_i`$ project $`i`$'s start years:

Write your rows in "started by year $`t`$" terms, each with its quantifier and a label, before you code them. Decide which years $`t`$ each kind of row needs, and check the third rule against the years you chose.

A sum over no variables is the plain number 0 in Python, and MathOpt refuses a row with no variable on either side (a `TypeError` about a `bool`). Such a row says nothing, so either skip it or wrap each sum in `mathopt.LinearExpression(...)`, which MathOpt accepts even when it is empty.
The tests fix every `x[pid, t]` through its bounds and ask the solver whether the model accepts the plan, so any correct formulation passes. About ten lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    starts: tuple[int, ...]


def add_testing_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, projects: list[Project], years: tuple[int, ...],
                      testing: dict[str, tuple[str, int]]) -> None:
    """Testing never before its station, and started within k years of it inside the plan."""
    # TODO: the "not before" rows and the deadline rows.
    return None


def build(projects: list[Project], years: tuple[int, ...],
          testing: dict[str, tuple[str, int]]) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="testing")
    x = {(p.pid, t): model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}_{t}") for p in projects for t in p.starts}
    for p in projects:
        model.add_linear_constraint(sum(x[p.pid, t] for t in p.starts) <= 1, name=f"once_{p.pid}")
    add_testing_rules(model, x, projects, years, testing)
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    years = (2027, 2028, 2029)
    projects = [Project("SUB", years), Project("TEST", years)]
    model, x = build(projects, years, {"TEST": ("SUB", 1)})
    print(model.get_num_linear_constraints(), "rows")

cases.says: a station tested within its deadline is allowed, and a station never tested is refused
testing a station that is never built is refused
testing that starts in the station's own build year is allowed
testing that starts exactly on the deadline is allowed, and a year later is refused
a station whose deadline falls after the plan's last year may go untested in the plan

origin.section: A Maximum Lag Bounds the Child From Below

concepts: a maximum lag bounds the child's running total from below, with a switch when the child may be left out
